answer: We formalize a mechanism where dynamic opportunity-cost bonds enforce capital barriers, inducing a gale of liquidation if agents attempt identity replication. Through a subgame-perfect punishment matrix, the expected payoff of Sybil expansion converges to a negative spiral, ensuring that any grove of colluding nodes deviates to honest play. This strict Nash equilibrium validates that unilateral Sybil multiplication remains irrational under arbitrary network latency.
